title: Nashville SC vs Columbus Crew: decisive showdown in MLS
seoTitle: Nashville SC vs Columbus Crew: decisive MLS showdown
subtitle: Eastern Conference leader hosts a team in crisis in an MLS match
excerpt: Nashville SC, top of the Eastern Conference, faces Columbus Crew, a side trying to halt its slump, in a clash that highlights the gap in recent form.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Nashville SC is set to host Columbus Crew in a Major League Soccer fixture marked by a clear recent performance gap between the two sides. The match pits the Eastern Conference leader against an opponent looking to reverse a negative run and regain winning rhythm.

Columbus Crew's crisis

Columbus Crew finds itself in a delicate moment this season, having gone unbeaten in three MLS games after a 2-1 loss to CF Montreal. Interim coach Laurent Courtois says he wants to see how the group reacts both collectively and individually to this adverse stretch. Despite an impressive run in the Leagues Cup, where the team reached the quarter‑finals, domestic league woes have dropped the Crew to 12th place in the Eastern Conference.

Nashville SC at the top

On the other side, Nashville SC consolidates its position as Eastern Conference leader, enjoying a seven‑point cushion over its pursuers. The side has amassed 46 points in 20 games (14 wins, 4 draws, 2 losses), a total that ties the highest point tally recorded at this stage in MLS history. A recent 1‑0 victory over New York Red Bulls reinforced the lead, following an impressive win against Inter Miami.

Head‑to‑head history

Nashville SC has won the last two direct encounters with Columbus Crew, including a 1‑0 away win on March 14. Historically, Nashville had only two victories in the first ten meetings with the Crew. Neither team had ever recorded three consecutive wins over the other before this recent streak, marking a shift in the rivalry’s balance.

Offensive and defensive challenges

Columbus Crew is struggling offensively, posting an expected goals (xG) value of just 0.31 in the loss to Montreal. That was the second‑lowest xG the team has recorded in any MLS game over the past five years, surpassed only by the 0.22 logged against Nashville in March. On the defensive side, Nashville’s goalkeeper Brian Schwake is a key pillar, tied for second in MLS with nine consecutive clean‑sheet matches, totaling 14 across all competitions—a club record.

Logistical challenges

Beyond the Nashville game, Columbus Crew faces a demanding schedule. The team will travel to Carson, California, to face Club América in the Leagues Cup quarter‑finals, a venue considered hostile. After that commitment, the Crew returns to meet New England Revolution. Coach Courtois stresses the need to adjust mindset and tactical options amid these back‑to‑back challenges, aiming to learn from the squad’s reactions in the coming weeks.

With information from CBS Sports, Field Level Media.
